A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the dose-response curve to nebulized bronchodilators is shifted to the right in acutely ill asthmatics, and that higher doses than the standard should be considered in the treatment of hospitalized asthmatics in status asthmatics.
most hospitalized asthmatic patients respond to nebulized bronchodilator therapy, and a large fraction require higher albuteroid doses than the standard.

The main takeaway from our work is that
a single dose of nebulized Albuterol (2.5 mg) is not sufficient to treat most patients with acute asthma exacerbations.
the bronchodilatory effect of nebulized salbutamol (albuterol) in patients with acute severe asthma varies widely and is not predictable from baseline severity of obstruction.
